Walk

The 1939 Gold and the General

3 stops · about 2 h 30 min · on foot

September 1939: the gold reserves of the Bank of Poland, evacuated through Romania, reach Istanbul on the British ship Eocene and go on by train to Beirut, where French warships take them on to France. From Kabataş take the ferry to Kadıköy on the Asian shore and walk to Haydarpaşa station, then walk to the cemetery where General Marian Langiewicz, dictator of the January Uprising, lies.

Stops

  1. Kabataş – where the gold tanker Eocene anchored

    Beyoğlu · 1939

    While the ship lay at anchor here, diplomats argued over whether Poland's gold should go into the Ottoman Bank or on through the Dardanelles – with Germany pressing Turkey hard.

  2. Across the water: take the ferry to this stop.

    Haydarpaşa Station – where Poland's gold boarded the train

    Kadıköy · 1939

    By the time the German naval attaché reported to Berlin, Poland's gold had already been moved here from a British ship to a train bound for Syria.

  3. Grave of General Marian Langiewicz, Haidar Pasha Cemetery

    Üsküdar · 1866–1887

    For a few days in March 1863 he was dictator of the uprising – and he spent his last two decades in Istanbul as a modest railway clerk known as 'Langie Bey'.

On the map

Part of this walk is by ferry or public transport, so plan each leg from one stop to the next.
